surrogate.title: Surrogate (published-profile)
surrogate.summary: Event knots (time, altitude, velocity) from official vehicle brochures/user manuals, interpolated every 5 s and laid along a constant-azimuth rhumb line from the pad (azimuth from NOTAM/hazard areas or from target inclination). One assumption splits horizontal motion from the published profile. Where a vehicle has no published profile, a family stand-in (LM-3B from the CALT manual) is used and labelled. ILLUSTRATIVE, not telemetry. Falcon 9 flights use SpaceX webcast telemetry (altitude and speed vs time) from a past F9 Block 5 Vandenberg launch as the family profile, timed to the mission's published SpaceX event timeline.

sim.title: First-principles 3DOF sim
sim.summary: Point-mass ascent simulator: rotating WGS-84 Earth with J2 gravity, US76 atmosphere drag, pressure-dependent thrust, staging/boosters/fairing/coasts; vertical rise, pitch kick, gravity turn then linear-tangent guidance optimized (Nelder-Mead) to reach the target orbit along the launch azimuth. Stage parameters from OSINT, each number sourced, derived or labelled an assumption. ILLUSTRATIVE, not telemetry. Long March vehicles run in timeline mode: published ignition/cutoff/separation times are hard events, burn rates from published thrust/Isp, and remaining free parameters fitted (bounded least squares) to the CALT manual LM-3B profile (altitude within 3.4 km at all events). Falcon 9: Block 5 masses and Merlin thrust/Isp from open sources, stage-1 cutoff at the published MECO with the unburned remainder standing in for landing propellant; checked against SpaceX's SECO-1 time and Falcon 9 webcast telemetry.
